Let’s dive into Chapter One—Discovering Intention as a Universal Force.
Most of us grow up thinking intention’s just about willpower. You know, that mental push to check off your to-do list and get things done. But have you ever noticed how, in those rare, quiet moments between all the noise and demands of life, a much deeper question starts to bubble up? What if intention isn’t only something you summon from within? What if it’s bigger—a kind of force that’s actually woven into the universe, always flowing, whether you notice it or not?
This idea usually doesn’t land all at once. Picture someone sitting at their kitchen table, staring at a list of goals that never seem to get any closer. The more they try, the farther away those dreams seem to drift. Frustration kicks in. That old advice—just try harder—starts to feel pretty empty. And right there, in that uneasy space, something new starts to grow: Maybe there’s another way to face life’s challenges. One that doesn’t demand so much pushing and striving.
Seeing intention as a universal energy changes everything. Suddenly, it’s not just a tool for getting what you want. Instead, it’s this field of possibility, always present, always available. It isn’t tied to your past mistakes or your current circumstances. Imagine it as a steady current, flowing quietly beneath the surface of your everyday life—just waiting for you to notice and tap into it.
The thing is, most people miss this because we’re taught that effort alone shapes reality. But think about those stories you hear—people who let go of trying to control every outcome, and suddenly, they’re in the right place at the right time. They meet the perfect person, or an unexpected opportunity drops into their lap. That’s not just luck. It’s a glimpse of what happens when someone aligns with that wider flow of intention.
There’s a story of a parent who spent years worrying about their child’s future, trying to manage every detail. Only when they let go—trusting in something larger—did things start to fall into place. The child found their own path, and the parent discovered a sense of peace they’d never known before.
This shift—seeing intention not just as your personal tool, but as a universal force—marks the start of a whole new way of living. Suddenly, life feels more like a partnership. Struggle gives way to co-creation. The world stops looking like a wall of obstacles, and starts to reveal itself as a landscape full of possibilities.
Most people don’t see this field of intention because everyday life can be so loud and distracting. But once the idea takes root, it’s tough to ignore. The question shifts from, “How can I make this happen?” to “How can I align myself with the energy that makes everything possible?”
And in that shift, you find a whole new kind of empowerment—one that doesn’t come from force, but from genuine connection.
